rules.title: Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for At-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: Before issuing a notice to terminate a tenancy for an at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the landlord must first give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure. If the violation is not cured in time, the landlord may serve a three-day notice to quit. The landlord must also notify the Commission no later than three business days after notifying the tenant, once the Commission's submission portal has been running for 30 days.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to the Division who issue a termination notice for at-fault just cause.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 renders void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706; attempts to recover possession in violation of the Division make the landlord liable for wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times the actual economic damages.
rules.quoted_span: Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be amended.
rules.interaction_text: an opportunity to cure the violation under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be amended

rules.title: Notice to Tenant for No-Fault Just Cause Termination
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must give the tenant written notice at least 30 or 60 days before the proposed termination date, as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, in no less than 12-point font. The notice must describe the basis for termination, state the tenant's right to relocation assistance, and state the tenant's right to receive an offer to renew if the unit is offered again for rent within five years. The landlord must also notify the Commission no later than three business days after notifying the tenant, once the Commission's submission portal has been running for 30 days.
rules.key_value: at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to the Division who issue a termination notice for no-fault just cause.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 renders void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall give written notice to the tenant at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended, in no less than 12-point font.
rules.interaction_text: as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy, provide relocation assistance either as a direct payment equal to two months of actual rent (three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled) or as an equivalent rent waiver. A direct payment must be made within 15 days from the date of the notice.
rules.key_value: two months of actual rent under the tenant's lease in effect at the date of the notice; three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of residential rental property subject to the Division whose tenancy is terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of income or length of tenancy.
rules.penalty: Any landlord who fails to provide relocation assistance as required by section 98.0706(c) is liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages.
rules.quoted_span: Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.interaction_text: Any relocation assistance required by this Division shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, or other local law.

rules.title: Right to Offer to Renew After No-Fault Just Cause Termination
rules.requirement: If the unit is offered for rent within five years of an eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), the landlord must first offer to lease it in writing to the displaced tenant, if the tenant asked in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and provided a mailing or email address. The tenant has 30 days from receipt of the offer to accept.
rules.key_value: within five years of the date the tenant was evicted
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by a no-fault just cause termination under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4) who requested an offer in writing within 30 days of the termination notice.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 renders void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.

rules.title: Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout offer the landlord must give each tenant a written disclosure of their rights, and any buyout agreement must be in writing with required statements. A buyout agreement must be for more than the relocation assistance available under section 98.0706(c); otherwise it is void.
rules.key_value: greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c)
rules.coverage_text: Landlords making buyout offers to tenants in residential rental property.
rules.penalty: A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed, or one that does not strictly comply with section 98.0707(c)(1)-(4), is void.
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.
